title: A lane dropped from a batch never loses its files when it merges main
why: Finding, Oct 27 (c88's lane and the build advisor): batch #663 dropped c88 with a revert of its merge; when the lane later merged main, the revert silently deleted 11 of its 13 files, and only files both sides edited showed as conflicts.
note: Cause: rule git-integration-branch-merge drops a lane by a removal commit that then lands on main; a lane that merges main (no rebase) takes that removal. The c88 lane re-applied its diff (acd0882). Fixes: (a) drop a lane by rebuilding the batch branch without it, so no removal reaches main (the lane's pick, and mine); (b) the rule tells a dropped lane to re-apply its diff after it merges main and check that every file survives. Home: the rule and the merge tooling. Needs no answer. Port: yes; the rule is global. Placed ahead of c82, after c97 (triage, Oct 27): it recurs on every drop and loses work silently.
